Rohid - What is the cut at the Masters?

content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Rohid's PostRohidApril 6 at 10:20 PM · Shared with PublicWhat is the cut at the Masters?As the 90th Masters Tournament gets underway this week at Augusta National, one of the most talked-about moments arrives Friday afternoon: the 36-hole cut.The current rule, in place since 2020, is straightforward and unforgiving. After two rounds, only the top 50 players and ties advance to the weekend. Anyone outside that group, regardless of how close they are to the leaders, misses the cut and heads home. No “10-shot rule” applies anymore.This marks a tightening from earlier formats. The cut was introduced in 1957 as the low 40 and ties. From 1962 to 2012 it became low 44 plus anyone within 10 strokes of the lead. Between 2013 and 2019 the field expanded slightly to low 50 and ties plus those within 10 strokes. Augusta officials removed the 10-shot provision in 2020 to create a more elite weekend field With a projected 2026 field of approximately 91 players, the cut typically leaves around 50-60 golfers playing Saturday and Sunday, depending on ties. The average cut score historically sits near 148 (even par or slightly higher), though it varies with weather and course conditions The Masters cut remains stricter than most PGA Tour events, which usually advance the top 65 and ties. This policy ensures only the strongest performers after 36 holes get to chase the green jacket over the famed back nine on moving day and Sunday As play begins Thursday, every shot in the opening rounds carries extra weight—because at Augusta, missing the cut means your Masters week ends abruptly. #MastersTournament #endsabruptly #momentsarrives #carriesextraLikeComment LikeComment
